task: Add the eight new Coloring subjects as pure data against the subject contract that shipped in slice 1: penguin, chicken, cat, dog, snowman, gingerbread, hero and ninja. The Robot already exists and must not change.
context: Slice 1 shipped the contract. src/minigames/coloring/subjects/robot.js is the worked example and the only correct reference for the exact shape of a subject; src/minigames/coloring/subjectRegistry.js is where a subject is registered.

A subject supplies: id, category ('animal' | 'character'), zooSpecies (string or null), pieces (root piece FIRST), pivots {piece:{x,y}}, parents {piece: parentPiece|null}, depth {piece:number}, shapes [{id, piece, order, shape}], details {eyes, pupilRatio, marks}, personality {idle, startup, hop, celebrate, glow?} and liveScale.

Silhouette shapes today come in two kinds: rect(x, y, width, height, radius) and circle(cx, cy, r). A rounded rect whose radius is half its height is a capsule, which is what makes a good animal body or limb. Coordinates are normalised 0..1 over a square picture with y increasing DOWNWARD.

Detail marks are drawn as line art OVER the child's paint and come in four types: line {x1,y1,x2,y2}, circle {cx,cy,r}, arc {cx,cy,r,startAngle,endAngle,counterclockwise} and polygon/triangle {points:[{x,y}]}. Each takes optional fill, stroke and lineWidth, and each carries the `piece` it belongs to so the paper puppet cuts it with that piece.

personality drives the ONE shared animation engine in robotPuppet.js. Look at how the robot's personality maps onto poseFor and rotationsFor before authoring the others: idle takes root {sway, bob, tilt, tiltPhase, squash} and per-piece {base, bob, phase}; startup takes root {shake, shakeFrequency, lift, tiltFromShake, restSquash, bounceSquash} and per-piece {base, flare, bounce}; hop and celebrate take root {hopHeightScale, tilt, tiltScale} and per-piece {base, air, lagAir}, plus rotationScale, blink and glow.
The controller does not pick subjects yet - slice 3 adds the random rotation and the generic POWER wording. Registering the eight is enough here.
The registry test written in slice 1 loops over every registered subject, so these eight come under its geometry, bounds, pieces and category assertions the moment they are registered.
requirements: Eight new files under src/minigames/coloring/subjects/: penguin.js, chicken.js, cat.js, dog.js, snowman.js, gingerbread.js, hero.js, ninja.js, each default-exporting a deeply frozen subject exactly as robot.js does. Register all eight in subjectRegistry.js.

CATEGORY: penguin, chicken, cat and dog are category 'animal' with zooSpecies set to their own id, so a later Zoo pass can find them without guessing. robot, snowman, gingerbread, hero and ninja are category 'character' with zooSpecies null.

EVERY SUBJECT MUST BE ONE CONNECTED SHAPE. This is the lesson the robot already learned and records: shapes must overlap at every joint so the figure reads as one drawing and so the seams stay hidden when a limb swings. A figure whose head floats above its body is the defect to avoid.

Keep each picture a COLOURING BOOK PAGE, not an illustration: a handful of big continuous areas a child can scribble across, bold outlines, few pieces. Faces, buttons, icing, scarves, belts and fur tufts are detail marks drawn OVER the paint, never separate silhouette shapes - a separately fillable detail is a region, and regions are what turned an earlier robot into a worksheet.

Each figure stands on its own lowest silhouette point and should use most of the picture height (roughly y 0.03 to 0.95, like the robot) and be horizontally centred about x = 0.5. Do not leave a figure floating with empty space below it: the baseline is derived from the silhouette's lowest point, so a stray low shape becomes the ground.

PIECE COUNTS, kept deliberately low: penguin 5 (body, leftWing, rightWing, leftFoot, rightFoot); chicken 5 (body, leftWing, rightWing, leftLeg, rightLeg); cat 4 (body, frontLeg, backLeg, tail); dog 4 (body, frontLeg, backLeg, tail); snowman 3 (body, leftArm, rightArm); gingerbread 5 (body, leftArm, rightArm, leftLeg, rightLeg); hero 6 (body, leftArm, rightArm, leftLeg, rightLeg, cape); ninja 5 (body, leftArm, rightArm, leftLeg, rightLeg). `body` is the root in every case.

CAT AND DOG ARE SIDE-ON (the owner chose this): a cartoon animal in profile, which gives a strong silhouette and an obvious tail, with one visible front leg and one visible back leg. Do not attempt four-legged anatomy. The head is part of the body piece, as the robot's is.

HERO's cape is its own piece and must sit BEHIND the body (lowest shape order, most negative depth) so it reads as a cape rather than a bib. Its emblem is an original generic star on the chest - no existing superhero's costume, colours, logo or silhouette, and no weapon.
NINJA is a generic hood-and-sash outfit with visible eyes, a belt, gloves and boots, playful rather than threatening, with NO weapon and no franchise markings.
SNOWMAN has no legs: two or three stacked snowballs with simple stick arms, a carrot nose, coal buttons and a scarf. Its ground baseline is the bottom of the lowest snowball.

ANIMATION PERSONALITY, expressed only through the existing personality fields: penguin a waddle with a wing flap; chicken a head bob with a wing flap; cat and dog a small bounding hop with a tail sway or wag; snowman a wobble and bounce with no legs; gingerbread a large cheerful bounce; hero a confident heroic hop with the cape trailing; ninja a quick light hop with a small crouch. Every subject must be visibly itself in motion without any new engine code.
Only the ROBOT gets the antenna glow. Every other subject leaves `personality.glow` unset so no chicken grows a glowing antenna.
Blinking is fine for every subject, so each needs `details.eyes` and a `pupilRatio`.

liveScale sets relative living size in the room: chicken and cat small, dog small-medium, penguin, gingerbread, robot and ninja medium, hero medium, snowman medium-large. Keep the spread modest - all nine must stay readable under the existing room camera and must not break crowding or dialogue.

If, and only if, a subject genuinely cannot be drawn well from rects and circles, you may add ONE new silhouette kind ('ellipse') - added once and generically to shapeBounds, insideShape and pathSilhouette with its own tests, never as a special case for one subject. Prefer capsules (a rect with radius = height / 2) first.
constraints: The Robot must not change at all - not its shapes, its details, its personality, its geometry or its motion. It is the shipped reference.
Do NOT add subject selection, do NOT change which subject a round uses, and do NOT change the visible ロボットパワー wording. That is slice 3.
Do not touch the Zoo or the Restaurant. The Restaurant must keep receiving robot records only - savedRobots() already filters, and nothing here may widen it.
Do not add per-subject branches anywhere. If a subject needs behaviour the contract cannot express, say so in your summary rather than adding an if.
Do not add new engine states, new pose functions, or a second animation path. Personalities are data.
Hero and ninja must be original, child-friendly and weapon-free. No copyrighted character's costume, emblem, colour scheme or silhouette.
Keep every subject's detail marks sparse. If a figure needs more than about a dozen marks to read, the silhouette is wrong.
Edit files with your structured patch/edit tool. If a shell-based edit fails once because of quoting or escaping, switch to the structured mechanism - do not try another escaped variant.
Append one dated DESIGN_DECISIONS.md entry for this pass covering the piece counts, the side-on cat and dog, and the hero/ninja originality rule, each with what, why and the rejected alternative.
startingPoints: src/minigames/coloring/subjects/robot.js (the only correct reference for the contract)
src/minigames/coloring/robotRenderer.js (drawMark, for the four detail mark types)
src/minigames/coloring/robotPuppet.js (poseFor and rotationsFor, for what a personality can express)
tests: The existing registry loop must pass for all nine subjects: non-empty silhouette, bounds inside the picture, a root piece first, every shape owned by a declared piece, pivots for every piece, no NaN, valid piece texture bounds, a category.

Connectedness: every subject's silhouette is ONE connected mass. Sample the silhouette on a grid, flood fill from any filled cell, and assert every filled cell is reached. This is the assertion that catches a floating head or a detached tail, and it is the single most valuable test in this order.
Every piece owns at least one shape, and every non-root piece's shapes overlap its parent's shapes somewhere, so no limb is attached by nothing.
Each subject stands: its lowest silhouette point maps to world Y approximately 0 through the paper puppet, and each uses a reasonable share of the picture height.
Category and zooSpecies are exactly as specified for all nine, and only the robot declares a glow.
Every personality names only pieces that subject actually has - a rotation for a leg the snowman does not have is a silent no-op today and a bug later.
pickNextSubject over the real nine-subject registry: never an immediate repeat, and every subject is reachable across seeded runs.

behavioralAcceptance.note: The controller renders all nine blank colouring pages and all nine puppets in motion and judges whether each is recognisable. Do not attempt a browser run and do not claim one.
